channel.title: Replaced by AI Layoff Tracker
channel.description: Recent sourced AI layoff tracker entries.

item.title: Vodafone Germany AI layoffs, November 9, 2026
item.description: Vodafone Germany: 2,300 layoffs. Explicit AI cited. Vodafone Germany announced approximately 2,300 planned workforce reductions over the next two fiscal years. The company explicitly linked structural changes and increased AI use to lower operating and personnel costs, including automation in network troubleshooting, marketing and customer service. AI is one contributing factor alongside competitive pressure, a shrinking TV market, mobile-price competition and inflation, not a claim that every affected role is directly replaced by AI.

item.title: SoundHound AI AI layoffs, November 4, 2026
item.description: SoundHound AI: – layoffs. Explicit AI cited. SoundHound AI disclosed a restructuring plan reducing approximately 27% of its global workforce, with exact headcount undisclosed. Management identified AI and systems-driven operations as a $15 million component of a broader $120 million annualized cost-reduction program. LivePerson integration, overlapping team and vendor consolidation, cloud optimization and exits from noncore operations are additional factors; the entire workforce reduction is not attributed solely to AI.

item.title: NiCE AI layoffs, November 4, 2026
item.description: NiCE: 500 layoffs. Explicit AI cited. NiCE announced a planned reduction of approximately 5% of its global workforce, reported as around 500 employees, while explicitly linking its operating-model changes to greater efficiency through AI. The company is also reducing management layers, simplifying decision-making and redirecting resources toward growth priorities including CX AI innovation. The exact headcount is undisclosed; approximately 500 is a reported estimate, not a company-confirmed tally or evidence that AI directly replaces every affected worker.

item.title: Block AI layoffs, November 4, 2026
item.description: Block: – layoffs. AI-adjacent restructuring. Block notified employees of a separate November round of job cuts affecting Customer Operations, Risk Operations, and Learning & Content Operations, with Cash App and Square staff reported affected. The number of departures is undisclosed. The notice cited better tools for routine tasks but did not explicitly name AI; an earlier SEC filing describes a broader efficiency strategy including AI automation, prioritisation, performance management and team centralisation. This is not evidence that AI directly replaced every affected worker, and February's more than 4,000 cuts are not counted again.

item.title: Fiserv AI layoffs, November 3, 2026
item.description: Fiserv: 3,000 layoffs. AI-adjacent restructuring. Fiserv disclosed 3,000 employee and contractor reductions since June 2026, including a reduction of more than 10% in senior management. Its company-stated AI-everywhere efficiency strategy and Project Elevate transformation provide a broader AI connection, not confirmation that all 3,000 departures were direct AI replacements. November 3 is the disclosure date, not a new 3,000-person future round.

item.title: Virgin Media O2 AI layoffs, November 3, 2026
item.description: Virgin Media O2: – layoffs. AI-adjacent restructuring. Virgin Media O2 confirmed workforce reductions as part of a cost programme combining organisational delayering, greater AI adoption and digital channels. Press reports suggest thousands of cuts, potentially up to 4,000, but the company has not disclosed a final headcount figure; the tracker leaves the count unknown. AI is one company-stated efficiency lever alongside debt reduction and broadband-market pressures, not the sole cause of every cut.

item.title: SUSE AI layoffs, November 2, 2026
item.description: SUSE: 190 layoffs. Explicit AI cited. SUSE announced plans to reduce its global workforce by approximately 10%, or about 190 roles based on a reported 1,900 employees. In an internal memo reviewed by The Register, CEO Dirk-Peter van Leeuwen explicitly cited automation and AI, saying modern tooling permits less overhead and flatter reporting lines and has greatly diminished the requirement for some existing roles. The 190 figure is an estimate, not a disclosed exact tally of completed departures.

item.title: Comcast AI layoffs, October 30, 2026
item.description: Comcast: 994 layoffs. AI-adjacent restructuring. Comcast disclosed 994 planned job cuts across Pennsylvania, Washington, New Jersey and California during a broader organizational and cost transformation. Executives described simplification and accelerated AI adoption as parts of the same operating strategy, but did not say AI directly caused each eliminated position. The four-state figure is not a disclosed nationwide total. Comcast also plans more than 1,100 new positions; these are not netted against the announced cuts.

item.title: NatWest AI layoffs, October 30, 2026
item.description: NatWest: – layoffs. AI-adjacent restructuring. NatWest disclosed a net headcount decrease of around 1,000 full-time equivalents in Q3 2026 and a 1,400-FTE year-to-date reduction excluding the Evelyn Partners acquisition. Including roughly 2,200 acquired FTEs, total headcount rose by about 800 year-to-date. CEO Paul Thwaite acknowledged that AI is changing some roles, alongside broader transformation and changes in the business portfolio. These are net workforce movements, not a disclosed gross layoff count or 1,000 confirmed AI replacements; the AI-only share is unknown.

item.title: ING AI layoffs, October 29, 2026
item.description: ING: 400 layoffs. AI-adjacent restructuring. ING announced around 400 planned redundancies globally as it restructures Wholesale Banking, with organizational changes effective March 1, 2027. The formal announcement emphasizes simplification and a new client-service model, with around EUR 75 million in annual savings fully effective from 2028. CEO Steven van Rijswijk separately acknowledged AI as part of ING's efficiency and growth strategy in a Dow Jones interview. AI is not established as the sole or direct cause of these cuts; these are planned redundancies, not 400 confirmed AI replacements or completed departures.

item.title: Skydance AI layoffs, October 26, 2026
item.description: Skydance: – layoffs. AI-adjacent restructuring. Skydance offered eligible employees a one-time voluntary buyout following its Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition. Eligibility numbers and final departures are undisclosed; this is a voluntary separation program, not confirmed compulsory layoffs. Reuters reported merger-related cost and debt pressures. The Wall Street Journal placed the buyouts within broader pressure to shrink headcount while investing in AI. That AI connection is journalist-inferred, not company-stated: Skydance did not identify AI as the direct cause.

item.title: Microsoft AI layoffs, October 26, 2026
item.description: Microsoft: – layoffs. AI reorg or spending linked. Microsoft announced a voluntary exit offer for participating teams in four countries, with about 60,000 employees eligible according to CNBC. Final departures are unknown: eligibility is not a job-cut count, and this is not a compulsory layoff of 60,000 workers. Microsoft confirmed the program and said it helps organizations adapt staffing to changing needs; CNBC linked the move to balancing costly AI infrastructure investment with capital efficiency. The AI-spending connection is journalistic context, not company confirmation of direct AI replacement.

item.title: American Express AI layoffs, October 23, 2026
item.description: American Express: 3,500 layoffs. Explicit AI cited. American Express announced about 3,500 planned job cuts globally, described as roughly 5% of its workforce, and a $336 million restructuring charge. CFO Christophe Le Caillec explicitly said the restructuring would make AmEx leaner and prepare it for AI by reducing management layers and improving processes ahead of automation. AI is one element of a broader efficiency program; these are planned reductions, not 3,500 confirmed direct AI replacements.

item.title: Vermont Information Processing AI layoffs, October 20, 2026
item.description: Vermont Information Processing: 66 layoffs. AI-adjacent restructuring. Vermont Information Processing (VIP) announced cuts affecting 66 employees, confirmed by its October 20 Vermont WARN notice, or roughly 11% of its approximately 600 Vermont employees. An anonymous employee told Seven Days that management presented a streamlined, product-led model with AI front and center, following company-wide AI training and the acquisition of AI-focused Encompass Technologies. The AI connection is employee-reported and journalist-inferred, not company-confirmed causation: VIP cited organizational priorities and investment alignment without naming AI as the cause. These are not 66 confirmed direct AI replacements.

item.title: Kroger AI layoffs, October 12, 2026
item.description: Kroger: 3,000 layoffs. Automation / efficiency cited. Kroger announced approximately 3,000 corporate job cuts over the next three years. CEO Greg Foran tied the restructuring to adopting technology, reducing duplicative work and simplifying the organization; AP reported the cuts alongside expanded AI use. These are planned reductions, not completed layoffs. AI is part of the broader strategy, but Kroger did not identify an AI-only share or say every affected role would be directly replaced by AI.

item.title: Airtable AI layoffs, October 12, 2026
item.description: Airtable: – layoffs. AI-adjacent restructuring. New owner Bending Spoons announced departures for a large portion of Airtable's pre-acquisition team, with no exact number disclosed. Management emphasized smaller, faster-moving teams while outlining investment in core improvements and AI features. This is company-stated strategic restructuring alongside AI investment, not a claim that AI directly replaced the affected employees; multiple business priorities underpin the change.

item.title: Bird AI layoffs, October 12, 2026
item.description: Bird: 880 layoffs. Explicit AI cited. Bird, formerly MessageBird, disclosed a decline from more than 1,000 employees to 120 over roughly three years as it extensively automated operations. CEO Robert Vis explicitly linked AI to reduced specialist staffing needs and a preference for multidisciplinary, autonomous workers. This represents more than 880 net positions eliminated or vacated, not a new October 12 layoff round. The involuntary-layoff versus attrition split and an AI-only count were not disclosed; 880 is a conservative lower bound used for tracker totals.

item.title: HoneyBook AI layoffs, October 8, 2026
item.description: HoneyBook: 30 layoffs. Explicit AI cited. HoneyBook is cutting around 30 to 35 employees, approximately 14% of its workforce, with most affected employees in Israel. The company explicitly linked the restructuring to aligning its structure and workflows with the AI era and integrating AI into its product and customer value proposition. This is company-stated strategic restructuring, not a claim that AI directly replaced the affected workers. The tracker uses 30, the lower end of the reported range, for aggregate totals.

item.title: DNB Bank AI layoffs, October 6, 2026
item.description: DNB Bank: 400 layoffs. Explicit AI cited. DNB Bank announced about 400 full-time-equivalent (FTE) reductions in Technology & Services, scheduled for completion during Q4 2026. The company explicitly linked the restructuring to gains from AI agents, technology and digital solutions. This is a planned reduction, not a confirmed completed layoff count; DNB did not isolate an AI-only share of the approximately 400 FTEs.

item.title: Apple AI layoffs, September 29, 2026
item.description: Apple: – layoffs. AI-adjacent restructuring. Bloomberg reporting, covered by Reuters and specialist Apple publications, described recent engineering program-management cuts affecting several managers, including roughly six directors, and cutbacks in Siri, Vision Pro and AI-software teams as CEO John Ternus pursues a leaner organization in the AI era. Total jobs affected are undisclosed. The AI connection is journalist-linked, not company-stated causation; some managers can transfer internally before layoffs later in 2026.
